title: House rent parties and the stride pianist Rock
summary: His aunt gave rent parties with a hired stride pianist called Rock, and young Freddie moved the furniture.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Because, you know. One of the reasons I'm interested, you know -- I mean -- guys always said so few guys sort of -- came out of New York. You know, guys all came out of everywhere and came to New York.
Yeah. Yeah.
But, you know, there weren't all that many guys that came up in New York --
Mm hmm, mm hmm. Right.
--so you know, it's fairly interesting to know that in those mid-twenties, and everything -- you were coming up here, then.
Yes. Yes. Mm hmm. Mm hmm. Yeah. Right.
And, different guys were coming into New York.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
When did you hear the first piano player that knocked you out, like James P. or something? Can you remember? Willie the Lick?
No.
Do you remember any of that?
It goes back further than that.
Does it?
Yeah. First time I heard -- . See, my aunt used to have -- used to give house rent parties
Oh, she did?
Yeah. Well, yeah.
Yeah. Everybody did. Yeah.
It wasn't -- you had to pay the rent.
Yeah. Right.
And, she had a piano, in other words. And, she used to hire a guy to come in and play the piano.
Yeah.
And -- I'm trying to think of this guy's name. I think his name was Rock.
Rock?
Rock. He was a stride piano player. (laugh)
(laugh)
I know he just came by Rock. That's his name. So, he used to come in and play. Naturally I used to have to do all the chores like moving everything back --
Yeah.
-- you know, I had to go through all that scene --
(laugh)
Yeah.
But, I really enjoyed the way he played.
What would he do -- play all night? Just to have a couple of drinks, and keep playing?
My aunt would keep drinks on the piano for him, you know.
And, he'd keep playing all the time?
He'd keep playing and playing.
How about that. When you think that people play two sets for the gigs now.
Yeah. So far as the music end of it is concerned, I don't know what to say.
